title: openchart-conversation-retrieval 1.0
description: Canonical message schema for the one neutral conversation-retrieval contract that openChart owns (opensoft/openChart-spec change define-clinical-message-inbox, ruling 69). Each system that holds patient conversations implements it: HealthLinc for the conversations it holds (coach conversations, direct messages to the doctor and administrative threads) and medXfactory for medical-AI conversations. Retrieval by reference is required of every holder. Reply delivery, the delivery-failure callback and split are optional capabilities that a holder declares in capabilities.result; openChart never sends a message for a capability the holder has not declared. Each returned turn carries its turn_id, author type and source token, and an ai turn may carry its mode, disclosure code, model reference, advice-statement reference and emergency-guidance codes. A result may name the earlier conversation it began from, by an opaque reference that openChart never retrieves on its own and never uses to resolve a patient. A retrieve names the request it serves in request_ref. The result carries the patient's sharing-consent reference and always at least one request turn, which carries that request_ref and holds the request itself, never a placeholder. For a priority or urgent item the request turns are always shared on the urgent_escalation basis with the patient told; a holder may withhold other turns that consent does not allow. Conversation content travels only between a holder and openChart, never through openPractice. References carry no PHI. Every object is closed. message_id is the idempotency key and carries no PHI. Implementations are compatible exactly when they share the MAJOR version; a receiver refuses any other MAJOR with unsupported_major_version.

contractVersion.description: MAJOR.MINOR. Implementations are compatible exactly when they share the MAJOR version. A sender uses the highest 1.x MINOR that both sides have declared. A receiver refuses any other MAJOR with unsupported_major_version. A breaking change needs a new MAJOR and a new digest.

issuer.description: A deployment's configured, stable issuer identifier, unique across deployments and never derived from a host path. References are compared as (issuer, namespace, value) triples, never by value alone.

opaqueRef.description: Opaque reference. Carries no name, date of birth, contact detail, amount or clinical content.

personRef.description: Opaque reference to a clinician or a staff member, minted by the system that knows the person. Never derived from a name or a login.

holderToken.description: A system that holds patient conversations and implements this contract.

sourceToken.description: Registry of turn sources: the system that produced or relayed the turn. healthlinc: the patient app, including its coach and its red-flag checklist. medxfactory: medXfactory, including its medical AI. openpractice_agent: an openPractice agent's administrative answer. A token is added only in a MINOR version.

conversationRef.description: Reference to a conversation in the system that holds it: (holder issuer, holder token, value). The same shape as conversation_ref in openpractice-clinical-handoff/1.0.

requestRef.description: The holder's reference for the patient's request, as the handoff carried it (healthlinc_message_ref in openpractice-clinical-handoff/1.0).

originConversationRef.description: Reference to an earlier conversation, in the shape of conversationRef, whose value is an opaque token. It carries no name, date of birth, contact detail or other PHI, and it never resolves, links or files a patient.

ehrPatientRef.description: The openChart patient reference the holder keeps for the account behind the conversation, if any: (openChart issuer, openchart, value). openChart only compares it with the link it already holds; it never links or files on it alone.

errorCode.description: The contract's one set of coded reasons. Never free text.

failureReason.description: Why a reply the holder had accepted could not be delivered. A subset of errorCode.

capability.description: Optional capabilities a holder may declare. Conversation retrieval is required of every holder and is not listed.

authorType.description: Who wrote the turn. unknown: the holder cannot attribute it, and openChart never treats it as clinician-authored.

textContent.description: Plain text only in 1.0. No attachments.

answerTypeRef.description: The practice-approved, read-only answer type and version an openPractice agent used (AH-05 exception 1). Same shape as answerTypeRef in openpractice-agent-operations/1.0.

restrictionCode.description: A confidential-communication restriction code from the patient's applied instructions.

urgency.description: The item's applied urgency. Ordered routine < priority < urgent.

aiMode.description: The mode the practice's medical director set for the AI that wrote the turn (ruling 59). Same values as the mode in openchart-ai-clinical-record-write/1.0.

emergencyGuidanceCode.description: A neutral code for a kind of emergency guidance an ai turn gave. It asserts no medical specifics. A value is added only in a MINOR version.

aiIdentity.description: The identity of the AI that wrote an ai turn, as owner ruling 80 identifies an AI: its openWallet ID, plus the model and model version that produced the turn. The openWallet ID has the identifier shape of openWallet's wallet record, as the clinical-acts foundation's walletId gives it. It names the AI as the author of the turn, never a patient or a person, and nothing needs the wallet to be reachable to read the chart (owner ruling 183). openChart keeps an ai turn's text in the chart only when the turn carries this object and the holder's registration covers its openwallet_id; otherwise openChart shows the turn by reference only.

turn.description: One turn of the conversation, keyed by turn_id, with its author type and source.

turn_id.description: The holder's stable reference for the turn.

request_turn.description: True for a turn of the escalated request: what the patient or representative asked the doctor. Such a turn is authored by the patient or a representative, carries request_ref, and has text with at least one non-whitespace character. It holds the request itself as written, never a placeholder, summary or redaction marker.

request_ref.description: On a request turn, and only there: the request_ref of the conversation.retrieve this result answers. openChart refuses a result with result_mismatch when no request turn carries a matching request_ref.

in_reply_to.description: The turn_id this turn answers, if any.

shared_basis.description: Why the holder shares this turn: within the patient's sharing consent, confirmed by the patient, or as a turn that triggered an escalation. For a priority or urgent item, at least one request turn carries urgent_escalation.

approved_by.description: The staff member who approved an openPractice agent's drafted answer before it was sent.

reply_id.description: For a clinician turn: the reply_id of the reply.deliver that carried it.

ai_mode.description: Optional, ai turns only: the mode in force when the AI wrote the turn.

disclosure_code.description: Optional, ai turns only: the code of the AI disclosure the patient was shown with the turn, from the holder's catalogue of disclosure texts. Lowercase words joined by underscores, with an optional version suffix such as _v2. It is the same for every patient shown that text, and carries no name, date of birth or other PHI.

model_ref.description: Optional, ai turns only: the model identifier and version that wrote the turn, as one reference.

advice_statement_ref.description: Optional, ai turns only: the holder's reference to the version of the advice statement shown with the turn, for example a not-medical-advice statement.

emergency_guidance.description: Optional, ai turns only: the kinds of emergency guidance the turn gave, as codes. It never replaces the turn's text, which must be non-empty. A code is added only in a MINOR version.

ai_identity.description: Optional, ai turns only: the AI's openWallet ID, model and model version (owner ruling 80, part B). Without it, or with an openwallet_id the holder's registration does not cover, openChart never keeps the turn's text in the chart and shows it by reference only.

capabilitiesRequest.description: openChart asks a holder which contract versions and optional capabilities it supports.

message_id.description: Random UUID. It is the idempotency key: every retry reuses it. It never carries PHI.

capabilitiesResult.description: A holder declares its versions and its optional capabilities: in answer to capabilities.request, or unprompted whenever they change. The latest declaration by declared_at governs. openChart never sends a message for a capability the holder has not declared.

message_id.description: Random UUID. It is the idempotency key: every retry reuses it. It never carries PHI.

acked_message_id.description: The capabilities.request answered, when there is one.

capabilities.description: May be empty: a holder that declares nothing supports retrieval only.

conversationRetrieve.description: openChart asks the holder for a conversation by reference, for a routed clinical item. Every holder supports it.

message_id.description: Random UUID. It is the idempotency key: every retry reuses it. It never carries PHI.

handoff_id.description: The routing id of the item the retrieval serves.

request_ref.description: The offer's request reference (healthlinc_message_ref in openpractice-clinical-handoff/1.0), passed through unchanged. Every request turn of the result carries it, and at least one must match it.

urgency.description: The item's urgency when openChart asks. For priority or urgent, the holder must share the request turns on the urgent_escalation basis and tell the patient.

conversationResult.description: The holder returns the conversation's shareable turns, each with its turn_id, author type and source, under the patient's sharing consent. The result always carries at least one request turn: what the patient or representative asked, as written, never a placeholder. Every request turn carries request_ref, and a result in which no request turn's request_ref matches the retrieve's is refused with result_mismatch. For a priority or urgent item, the request turns are always shared on the urgent_escalation basis and the patient is told, whatever else the patient's consent withholds. A holder may withhold other turns that consent does not allow, and then reports how many it withheld. A result that does not answer its retrieve is refused with result_mismatch.

message_id.description: Random UUID. It is the idempotency key: every retry reuses it. It never carries PHI.

urgency.description: The urgency the holder applied: the urgency of the conversation.retrieve it answers.

consent_ref.description: The holder's reference to the patient's sharing consent it applied.

snapshot_ref.description: Identifies the version of the conversation returned, so openChart can record which exchange the clinician saw.

turns_withheld.description: Optional. How many turns the patient's sharing consent kept back. A count only.

patient_told_at.description: When the patient was told that turns were shared for an escalation. Required when the urgency is priority or urgent, and whenever any turn has shared_basis urgent_escalation.

origin_conversation_ref.description: Optional. The earlier conversation this one began from, at the same holder or another, with an opaque value. openChart never retrieves it on its own, and never uses it to resolve, link or file a patient; reading it is a separate retrieval from the holder it names, under that holder's consent rules.

replyDeliver.description: openChart sends a clinician's reply for delivery to the patient. Only to a holder that declared reply_delivery. The holder answers with message.ack: received means accepted for delivery.

message_id.description: Random UUID. It is the idempotency key: every retry reuses it. It never carries PHI.

reply_id.description: openChart's id for the reply, reused on every retry.

reply_path_ref.description: The handoff's reply_path_ref, passed through unchanged.

channel_restrictions.description: Restriction codes that apply to the reply and to any notification for it. May be empty.

delivery_scope.description: conversation_only: deliver inside the conversation that carried the request, and use no other channel.

replyDeliveryFailed.description: The holder reports that a reply it had accepted could not be delivered. Only from a holder that declared delivery_failure_callback. openChart answers with message.ack.

message_id.description: Random UUID. It is the idempotency key: every retry reuses it. It never carries PHI.

reply_message_id.description: The message_id of the reply.deliver message.

splitRequest.description: openChart asks the holder to split a mixed item and resubmit only its administrative part to openPractice as a new inquiry. Only to a holder that declared split. The holder answers with message.ack: received means it has taken on the split.

message_id.description: Random UUID. It is the idempotency key: every retry reuses it. It never carries PHI.

messageAck.description: Acknowledges reply.deliver, reply.delivery_failed, split.request and an unprompted capabilities.result, and carries the coded refusal of any message, conversation.retrieve included. A refusal changes nothing.

message_id.description: Random UUID. It is the idempotency key: every retry reuses it. It never carries PHI.
